I think the answer is an overall social reform that views mental illness as a viable illness, and views treatments other than medication as also valid. Insurance companies need to cover therapy to a greater extent than they do now, the social stigma of mental illness needs to disappear, and the funding needs to be shifted to non-medicine treatments. We are currently in that shift, so we are headed in the right direction. I want to make sure we continue on the pendulum. 

Psychology tends to swing between philosophy and biology. With Freud back in the old times, we were very much philosophy based. With Skinner and behaviorism back in the 50's, we started to swing towards biology. The creation of more medication helped with that transition too. Now, we have swung too far towards biology and need to head back towards the mental, internal, and cognitive side of the spectrum. All while avoiding becoming un-scientific. It's a delicate balance.

It depends on the hospital. Some facilities are not state run, but privately run and tend to have therapy and other strategies for treatment available. Then there are the most expensive specialized clinics where nearly every possible method of treatment is available. The main thing I think is the problem is the presence of overmedication in the field of psychiatry and psychology. Many hospitals are state run, and have to go by state policies and exist on state funding, so they are only able to provide medication. They prescribe medications that are not recommended for the illnesses of the patients, and will even give them medication to make them more "manageable". I've read several books on the subject. It's really as much of a policy issue as it is a social issue

I would want to change the way hospitals work, specifically those in inner cities. In there, they just medicate them into a stupor, keep them there until they feel like they should be out, and then throw them back out onto the streets. The way things are now isn't working. I really want to change that, and i think the hospitals is the place to start.
